verdict.rationale: Navan documents an OAuth 2.0 client-credentials flow for its API, which lets a user issue machine credentials that an agent could use. Its MCP server also lets AI assistants connect to Navan data. However, nothing in the evidence shows that these credentials can be scoped, restricted to read-only, or otherwise limited to least privilege. Missing for 10: documented OAuth scopes or per-credential permission restrictions, read-only versus write separation for agent access, credential lifecycle controls (rotation and revocation), and independent or hands-on corroboration.
